title: Cultural Revolution
summary: A social upheaval in the People's Republic of China that began as a struggle between Mao Zedong and other top Communist Party leaders for dominance and then affected the whole country. Red Guards attacked perceived opponents, and the movement lasted from 1966 to 1976, leaving deep scars on Chinese society.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on 1966-1976 as the span; the Stanford page notes armed clashes ended in summer 1968 and order returned.

where.modern_name: Beijing, China (pin is a proxy: the capital, where the movement's mass rallies and early events took place; the movement covered all of China)

importance.justification: A decade-long upheaval that affected all of China and shaped its politics.

audience_note: Concerns political persecution and violence, including beatings, suicides and deaths from injuries.

sources.title: Introduction to the Cultural Revolution
sources.publisher: Stanford Program on International and Cross-Cultural Education (SPICE), Stanford University
